name: DPRK deceptive IT employment as a proliferation-finance risk control

attribution.legal_posture: Official regional or global policy/defensive context; named incident, person attribution, seizure, and adjudication status remain unreported.

caveats: Use this as an official regional-policy citation supporting the inclusion of DPRK deceptive IT employment in proliferation-finance risk programs; its scope is the already cataloged March 2024 alert.
The source adds source-level context; named worker, facilitator, company, wallet, transaction, seizure, and recovery outcomes require separate evidence.

statements: APG's 2025 typologies report places Japan's March 2024 alert to companies and organizations regarding North Korean IT workers inside a section summarizing Japan's proliferation-financing risks and mitigating measures.
The same passage groups the alert with asset-freezing readiness for crypto-asset exchanges and financial institutions, expansion of the crypto travel rule, and export-control updates.
The report does not supply a new worker, employer, facilitator, front company, payment flow or enforcement event.
limitations: Suitable as an official regional-policy citation supporting the proposition that DPRK deceptive IT employment belongs in proliferation-finance risk programs. Do not present it as a new incident or new Japanese measure beyond the already cataloged March 2024 alert.
APG places the Japanese alert within a proliferation-financing mitigation framework. This policy context is not an observed incident.
